title: The New Deal
examples: What were the main goals of the New Deal programs?
Did the New Deal solve all the problems of the Great Depression?
How did the New Deal change the role of the federal government?

explain.say: The New Deal was a set of programs started by Franklin Roosevelt. It aimed to help America during the Great Depression. These programs tried to restore the economy and give jobs to people.

items: Roosevelt takes office: New Deal begins
Programs implemented: Job creation and relief

explain.say: One key programme was the Civilian Conservation Corps. This group put young men to work on conservation projects. They helped plant trees and improve national parks across the country.

draw.text: CCC: Conservation jobs for young men

explain.say: Another important area was banking. The government created the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation. This insured your bank deposits, making people trust banks again.
The Agricultural Adjustment Administration aimed to raise crop prices. It reduced the supply of certain crops to help farmers earn more money. This was a direct attempt to boost farm income.
In everyday life, think about building a new bridge. The government might fund a job program to employ workers. This uses the same idea of public work for economic benefit.
A common mistake is thinking the New Deal fixed everything immediately. In reality, the Great Depression was a huge problem. The New Deal helped greatly, but full recovery took many years.

faq.q: Did the New Deal solve the Great Depression completely?
faq.a: No, it did not solve it completely. While it provided massive relief and recovery, the full recovery was a long process.
asks: Was the Great Depression over because of the New Deal?
Did the US economy return to normal right away?

faq.q: What was the main purpose of the Civilian Conservation Corps?
faq.a: Its main purpose was to provide employment for young men while also improving the country's natural resources. They worked on conservation projects.
asks: What kind of jobs did the CCC give out?
Was the CCC only about planting trees?

faq.q: How did the FDIC help people's savings?
faq.a: The FDIC insured bank deposits, which meant the government guaranteed your money up to a certain amount if the bank failed. This built public trust.
asks: Why did people lose trust in banks?

faq.q: Was the New Deal only for farmers?
faq.a: No, it covered many areas. It addressed banking, labor, and conservation, not just agriculture. Farmers were certainly helped, but it was much broader.
asks: Did the AAA only help farmers?
Were city workers also covered by the New Deal?

faq.q: Who was the main leader behind these changes?
faq.a: Franklin Roosevelt was the President who championed and oversaw the implementation of these major New Deal programs. He guided the nation through the crisis.
asks: What was Roosevelt's role in the New Deal?

facts: The New Deal was a series of programs enacted between 1933 and 1938.
It aimed to provide relief, recovery, and reform to the American economy.
The Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) provided jobs in conservation work.
The FDIC was created to restore confidence in the banking system.

quiz.say: Which program focused on preserving natural resources like forests and parks?
quiz.why: The CCC was specifically designed to put young men to work on environmental improvement and conservation projects.

wrong.0: While related, the CCC is the specific program mentioned for conservation work.
wrong.2: This program dealt only with protecting money saved in banks, not with physical resources.
wrong.3: This program focused only on controlling the supply and price of farm crops.

quiz.say: If a bank failed, which agency protected the money of the average citizen?
quiz.why: The FDIC was established to insure deposits, giving people confidence to use banks again.

wrong.0: This is a group of people, not a specific insurance agency.
wrong.2: The CCC dealt with physical labor and conservation, not financial safety.
wrong.3: The AAA was concerned with stabilizing the prices of agricultural goods.

quiz.say: The New Deal's overall success is best described as:

options.show: It ended the Great Depression instantly.
options.say: It ended the Great Depression instantly.

options.show: It only helped farmers and workers.
options.say: It only helped farmers and workers.

options.show: It required no further government action.
options.say: It required no further government action.

options.show: Providing vital immediate relief and setting up modern regulatory systems.
options.say: Providing vital immediate relief and setting up modern regulatory systems.

quiz.why: It successfully provided immediate help and created lasting structures, though full recovery was gradual.

wrong.0: Economic recovery was a long, complex process that took years to stabilize fully.
wrong.1: Its scope was much wider, impacting banking, industry, and infrastructure.
wrong.2: The need for continued oversight and reform meant government involvement remained high.
